quandoUsar: Height-limited lists inside cards, menus, or panels, with `maxHeight`, where thick native bars would be heavy.
Horizontal strips of chips or filters (`orientation="horizontal"`), where the vertical mouse wheel scrolls sideways while there is room.
Strips with native snapping via `snap`, without replacing system scrolling with a simulated one.
quandoEvitar: Use `message-scroller` for conversations that need to follow new messages.
Use `carousel` when the strip needs arrows, indicators, and an active slide.
For scrolling the whole page, let the browser scroll; the area is meant for inner regions.

teclado.acao: Scroll the content on the axes that scroll, when the area is focused; the scrolling is the browser's native one.
Scroll one page at a time.

acessibilidade: The scroll viewport always enters the Tab order; with `label`, it becomes a named `region`, so always pass a `label` so it is not an unnamed focus stop.
The drawn bars are hidden from the screen reader; scrolling stays native, so keyboard, touch, and assistive technologies work as on the platform.
movimento: The bars appear on scroll or pointer hover and fade out after `hideDelay` (900 ms); the thumb thickens under the cursor.
Each edge fades only when there is content beyond it, growing over the first pixels of scroll up to `fade` px (default 28; 0 turns it off).
Clicking the track scrolls 90% of the visible area with a smooth animation, which becomes a jump with “reduce motion” on; the bar transitions are also turned off.
responsivo: On touch screens, without a hovering pointer, the bars only appear during scrolling; `scrollbars="always"` keeps them visible when there is overflow.
The area only scrolls with a limited height: pass `maxHeight` or give the parent a height.
desempenho: Scrolling does not re-render React: bars and fades are written straight to the DOM, and a `ResizeObserver` together with a `MutationObserver` tracks changes in the content.
notasIA: Use `onEdgeChange` to know when the end has been reached, for example to load more, and `viewportRef` to scroll from code.
With `snap`, set `scroll-snap-align` on the children; the component only forwards the value to the viewport's `scroll-snap-type`.
